scope: Indiana adult education, workforce, reentry, community development, foster youth, disability employment, and youth training resources

records.name: The Excel Center Indiana
records.description: Tuition-free public charter high school for Indiana adults and older youth who have not earned a high school diploma, with flexible year-round classes, life coaching, free college credit, industry credentials, child care at some sites, and transportation support.
records.availability_notes: Applicants must live in Indiana and lack a high school diploma. Programs are generally in person; schedules and support services vary by campus. Verified August 6, 2026.

records.name: Fathers and Families Center
records.description: Indianapolis organization supporting fathers through parenting education, employment and career services, construction training, HSE preparation, couples support, and reentry programming.
records.availability_notes: Participants generally complete the Strong Fathers program before entering several advanced programs. Cohort schedules and eligibility should be confirmed. Verified August 6, 2026.

records.name: Martindale Brightwood Community Development Corporation
records.description: Provides youth employment services, income-based homeowner repair, affordable-housing and neighborhood development, small-business readiness, grant and certification navigation, and community education in Martindale-Brightwood.
records.availability_notes: Home repair is income-based and first come, first served. JumpStart and other cohort programs have limited application windows. Verified August 6, 2026.

records.name: Mary Rigg Neighborhood Center
records.description: Southwest Indianapolis center offering employment coaching, HSE and ELL, vocational pathways, basic-needs and food support, financial coaching, youth enrichment, after-school care, and summer programming.
records.availability_notes: Youth programs may use waitlists, sliding-scale fees, school-specific transportation, and CCDF. Training cohorts and pantry schedules should be rechecked. Verified August 6, 2026.

records.name: Foster Success
records.description: Supports teens and young adults with foster-care experience through education funding, workforce credentials, career coaching, financial empowerment, basic-needs navigation, health support, and youth leadership.
records.availability_notes: Eligibility varies by program and generally depends on age and foster-care history. Some workforce programs are limited to specified Central Indiana counties. Verified August 6, 2026.

records.name: Indiana Plan Apprenticeship Readiness Program
records.description: Statewide pre-apprenticeship program preparing Hoosiers for union building-trades careers through math, OSHA 10, life skills, interview preparation, apprenticeship navigation, and placement support.
records.availability_notes: Typical entry requirements include age 18+, diploma or HSE, Indiana driver's license, reliable transportation, TABE readiness, and drug screening. Verified August 6, 2026.

records.name: Erskine Green Training Institute
records.description: Postsecondary vocational training for people with disabilities in hospitality, food service, healthcare, inventory distribution, manufacturing, workplace behavior, independent living, and internships.
records.availability_notes: Programs are cohort-based and may be residential or commuter depending on site. Admissions, tuition, financial aid, and current training tracks should be verified. Verified August 6, 2026.

records.name: Freedom Academy Continuing Education
records.description: Northeast Indiana continuing-education provider offering HVACR, welding, CNA, CCMA, CNC machining, QMA, CAD, leadership, safety, manufacturing, and customized employer training.
records.availability_notes: Courses, tuition, prerequisites, certification testing, and tuition assistance vary by class and session. Verified August 6, 2026.

records.name: The Arc of Evansville
records.description: Provides services for children, students, young adults, and adults with disabilities, including vocational training, work services, skill development, supported opportunities, and pathways toward community employment.
records.availability_notes: Program eligibility, referral processes, capacity, work setting, and funding source vary by service. Verified August 6, 2026.

records.name: YouthBuild Evansville
records.description: Year-round education and workforce program for eligible Evansville youth ages 16-24 combining HSE or diploma completion, construction pre-apprenticeship, NCCER credentials, leadership, community service, weekly pay, and post-program employment support.
records.availability_notes: Typical eligibility includes age 16-24, Evansville residency, low income, no diploma or HSE, interest in construction, and drug-free participation. Enrollment documentation and cohort capacity should be confirmed. Verified August 6, 2026.
